meta.title: CAI: UI built for accessibility on native HTML, no framework
meta.description: CAI (Consistent Adaptive Identity) is a CSS-first, zero-build design system for the web: tokens, components and page layouts on native HTML, three color modes, one cascade layer you can always override, and JavaScript only as an enhancement.

hero.title: CAI, a native, styled design system built for accessibility.
hero.lead: A CSS-first, zero-build design system for the web. Three color modes, your CSS always wins, JavaScript only as an enhancement.
what.title: Why teams use CAI
what.lead: For sites and tools that should work for everyone, on any device, for years, without a framework to keep up with.
what.nojs.title: Works without JavaScript
what.nojs.text: Components are native HTML elements: <dialog>, <details>, form controls, popovers. JavaScript only adds polish, so pages keep working when a script fails.
what.a11y.title: Built for accessibility
what.a11y.text: Keyboard support, visible focus, 4.5:1 text contrast and a high-contrast mode are part of every component, and automated checks run on every change. The accessibility statement lists what has not been tested yet, screen readers included.
what.install.title: Nothing to install to try it
what.install.text: Plain CSS and small ES modules from a CDN or npm. No preprocessor, no compiler, zero dependencies: what you read in the files is what the browser runs.

adopt.title: Adopt it one layer at a time
adopt.lead: One direction: each package needs the ones below it and nothing above it, and installing it brings them in. Pick the level you need and stop there.
adopt.level1.title: Tokens only
adopt.level1.when: Choose this if you already have components or a framework and only want consistent values and color modes.
adopt.level1.colors: 53 color primitives in 7 families
adopt.level1.semantic: 55 semantic tokens, each defined for light, dark and high contrast
adopt.level1.scales: Spacing (12), control heights (4), type sizes (9), radii (6) and shadows (3)
adopt.level1.fonts: ET Book for running text and headings, self-hosted and MIT licensed; the system fonts for controls, labels and code
adopt.level1.contrast: A contrast check for your own colors, as a command or in the browser
adopt.level2.title: Tokens + Core
adopt.level2.when: Choose this if you are building pages or an app and bring your own page layout.
adopt.level2.components: 25 components: buttons, forms, tables, tabs, modal, media player and more
adopt.level2.objects: 7 layout objects, a small set of utilities and the styles of bare HTML elements
adopt.level2.js: Optional JavaScript for tabs, modals, copy buttons and players; every page works without it
adopt.level2.print: Print styles and right-to-left layouts, with no extra file
adopt.level2.layer: Everything in one cascade layer, cai: your own CSS wins without !important
adopt.level3.title: Tokens + Core + Site
adopt.level3.when: Choose this if you build whole sites and want the page shell, header, footer and search. This landing is built at this level.
adopt.level3.shell: Page, main, content and section wrappers with a consistent vertical rhythm
adopt.level3.parts: Page header, action group, feature grid, image frame and footer
adopt.next.title: Next: a package for your kind of site
adopt.next.lead: Packages for one kind of site build on site. Install the one at the top: it brings everything below it.
adopt.next.cms: cms: a blog, a newspaper or any CMS, built with any stack. Article header, post lists, table of contents and author box.
adopt.next.landing: landing: a landing page. Feature grid, speakers and calls to action.
adopt.next.wordpress: wordpress: a WordPress site. The cms package fitted to the block editor, a theme.json made from the tokens and base templates to copy.
fit.title: When CAI fits
fit.good.public: Content sites, documentation and public services that must meet WCAG 2.2 AA.
fit.good.server: Server-rendered pages and static sites, in any back-end language.
fit.good.own: Teams that want to read and own their CSS.
fit.bad.react: You need ready-made React or Vue components.
fit.bad.grid: You need a data grid, charts or a date-range picker: CAI has none.
fit.bad.beta: You need a stable API today: CAI is in beta, and names can still change.
